name: Vienna
operatingHours: U-Bahn runs ~5:00 AM–~12:30 AM daily, every 2–8 min by day. On Friday and Saturday nights and the night before public holidays all five lines run through the night every ~15 min; other nights NightLine buses take over.
fareInfo: A single ticket is €3.20 at machines (€3.00 in the WienMobil app, 2026) and covers any trip within Vienna with unlimited transfers in one direction. 24-hour pass €10.20 (€9.70 digital), 7-day pass €28.90 (€25.20 digital); 48- and 72-hour passes were withdrawn in 2026. No gates, but tickets are checked: validate paper tickets before boarding. City tickets don't cover the airport: ÖBB trains cost €5.50 into Vienna, the CAT express €14.90.

Hotel Imperial, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Vienna
Ruby Sofie Hotel Vienna by IHG

sights.name: Schönbrunn Palace
sights.note: The Habsburgs' Baroque summer palace with 40 state rooms open to visitors and vast formal gardens climbing to the Gloriette.
sights.hours: State rooms ~8:30 AM–5:30 PM daily (to 5:00 PM Nov–Mar, 6:30 PM Jul–Aug); gardens from 6:30 AM, free

sights.name: Kunsthistorisches Museum Vienna
sights.note: The imperial art collection under a grand cupola: Bruegel, Vermeer, Raphael, Titian and an Egyptian wing. Time-slot tickets only from September 2026.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–6:00 PM daily, till 9:00 PM Thu

sights.name: Belvedere Museum
sights.note: Two Baroque palaces linked by terraced gardens; the Upper Belvedere holds Klimt's The Kiss and other Austrian masterpieces.
sights.hours: Upper Belvedere 9:00 AM–6:00 PM daily; Lower Belvedere 10:00 AM–6:00 PM

sights.name: St. Stephen's Cathedral
sights.note: Vienna's Gothic landmark with a patterned tile roof; climb the 343-step south tower or tour the catacombs.
sights.hours: ~6:00 AM–10:00 PM (Sun from 7:00 AM); tourist visits limited during services

sights.name: The Hofburg
sights.note: The sprawling imperial palace: the Imperial Apartments, Silver Collection and Sisi Museum, which reopens redesigned on 19 November 2026.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–4:30 PM daily until 18 Nov 2026 (Sisi Museum closed); longer hours after reopening

sights.name: Austrian National Library (State Hall)
sights.note: A soaring Baroque library hall of frescoes, marble and 200,000 old volumes off Josefsplatz.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–6:00 PM, till 9:00 PM Thu; closed Mon Oct–May

sights.name: Tiergarten Schönbrunn (Vienna Zoo)
sights.note: The world's oldest zoo, founded in 1752 in the Schönbrunn grounds, now home to giant pandas and a rainforest house.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–4:30 PM Nov–Jan, to 6:30 PM Apr–Sep (varies by month)

sights.name: Albertina
sights.note: A Habsburg palace on the old city bastion with lavish state rooms and a modern collection from Monet to Picasso.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–6:00 PM daily, till 9:00 PM Wed & Fri

sights.name: Wiener Staatsoper
sights.note: The Vienna State Opera on the Ring: book a performance, grab a cheap standing ticket, or take a backstage guided tour.
sights.hours: Guided tours most days; performances evenings Sep–Jun

sights.name: Prater & Giant Ferris Wheel
sights.note: A huge public park with an old-school funfair at its edge, crowned by the 1897 Riesenrad Ferris wheel.
sights.hours: Park always open; Ferris wheel ~10:00 AM–9:45 PM (shorter in winter)

sights.name: Naturhistorisches Museum Wien
sights.note: The natural history twin of the art museum across the square: dinosaurs, meteorites and the 29,500-year-old Venus of Willendorf.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–6:00 PM, till 8:00 PM Wed, closed Tue

sights.name: Leopold Museum
sights.note: The world's largest Egon Schiele collection plus Klimt and Viennese Secession design, inside the MuseumsQuartier.

sights.name: Peterskirche
sights.note: A jewel-box Baroque church just off the Graben with a green oval dome and frequent free organ recitals.
sights.hours: Mon–Fri 7:00 AM–8:00 PM, Sat–Sun 9:00 AM–9:00 PM

sights.name: Hundertwasserhaus
sights.note: A wavy, multicoloured council housing block with trees on its roofs, designed by artist Friedensreich Hundertwasser.
sights.hours: Exterior viewable any time (residential, no entry)

sights.name: Vienna City Hall (Rathaus)
sights.note: A neo-Gothic city hall whose square hosts the Christmas market, an ice rink and summer film festivals.
sights.hours: Free guided tours Mon, Wed & Fri at 1:00 PM (except during sessions); square always open

sights.name: Imperial Crypt (Kapuzinergruft)
sights.note: The burial vault of the Habsburgs beneath the Capuchin church, with ornate tombs of Maria Theresa, Franz Joseph and Sisi.

sights.name: Naschmarkt
sights.note: Vienna's long open-air food market along the Wienzeile, with produce stalls, deli counters and cafés; a flea market joins on Saturdays.
sights.hours: Mon–Fri 6:00 AM–7:30 PM, Sat 6:00 AM–5:00 PM, closed Sun

sights.name: Kahlenberg
sights.note: A wooded hilltop in the Vienna Woods with a free terrace view over the city, the Danube and the vineyards below; bus 38A from Grinzing.

railStations.name: Wien Hauptbahnhof
railStations.note: Vienna's main station: Railjets to Salzburg, Innsbruck, Munich, Zurich, Graz, Budapest, Prague and Venice, Nightjet sleepers, and fast trains to the airport (~15 min). U1 to Stephansplatz in 4 min.
railStations.hours: Station open 24 h. Mainline trains run to individual timetables.

airports.name: Vienna International Airport
airports.transitNote: ÖBB Railjet/REX7 to Wien Hauptbahnhof in ~15–20 min (€5.50). The CAT express runs non-stop to Wien Mitte in ~16 min (€14.90). The S7 currently ends at St. Marx because of trunk-line works until ~Oct 2027. None of these are on the U-Bahn map.
airports.hours: CAT from airport: first 6:10 AM, last 11:37 PM. ÖBB trains run ~5:00 AM–~midnight.
